title: Expose Tide (Screen 1) trend per historical bar in GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators
description: docs/ideas.md's first entry (chart shading of Screen 1 bull/bear/neutral regions) needs `tide.trend` per historical bar, but `IndicatorHistoryPoint` (backend/app/api/schemas.py) only ever projects out signal/confidence/indicators/wave fields today, even though `analyse_history()` (backend/app/signals/engine.py) already recomputes Screen 1 fresh for every bar (via `_weekly_through_bar_date`) as part of its own per-bar `SignalResult`. This is pure plumbing -- no new computation -- add a `tide_trend` (or nested `tide`) field to `IndicatorHistoryPoint`, sourced from each bar's already-computed `screens['tide']['trend']`. This is the backend prerequisite for the tide-region chart-shading frontend task; nothing else currently blocks it.

checklist.step: Decide the exact field shape (flat `tide_trend: 'BULLISH'|'BEARISH'|'NEUTRAL'` vs a nested `tide` object matching the /analysis response's own screens.tide shape) and record as a decisions entry -- prefer consistency with the existing /analysis schema unless there's a good reason not to.
Add the field to IndicatorHistoryPoint in backend/app/api/schemas.py, sourced from analyse_history()'s existing per-bar result.
Unit test covering a ticker whose historical Tide trend actually changes across the returned range (not a fixture that's constant BULLISH throughout, which wouldn't catch a wiring bug).
Confirm the last point in the response still matches GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis's own screens.tide.trend for the same ticker/date, per this endpoint's existing documented invariant.

decisions.decision: Added a nested `tide: TideScreen` object to `IndicatorHistoryPoint` (reusing the exact same `TideScreen` model -- `trend` + `weekly_macd_histogram_slope` -- that `AnalysisResponse.screens.tide` already uses), sourced per-bar from `result.screens["tide"]` via the same `cast(TideScreen, ...)`-for-mypy-only pattern `get_analysis` already uses for `screens=cast(Screens, result.screens)`/`indicators=cast(Indicators, result.indicators)`. The field is never null (unlike stochastic_k/channel_upper/rsi/season): `evaluate_tide` always returns a concrete trend ('NEUTRAL'/'flat' rather than an absent value) even with insufficient weekly history, so there's no warm-up-null case to model here.
decisions.rationale: Rejected the flat `tide_trend: 'BULLISH'|'BEARISH'|'NEUTRAL'` alternative from the checklist: it would drop `weekly_macd_histogram_slope`, which the /analysis response's own screens.tide already exposes alongside trend specifically so a client can distinguish a genuinely-flat slope from a slope that was overridden to NEUTRAL by a disagreeing EMA relationship (see evaluate_tide's own docstring) -- the chart-shading consumer this task exists for may well want that same distinction for a tooltip/legend, and there's no cost to keeping it since analyse_history() already computes and carries weekly_macd_histogram_slope through unchanged. Nesting under `tide` (rather than flattening both fields with a `tide_` prefix) directly reuses the existing `TideScreen` Pydantic model instead of duplicating its two fields, keeping the two endpoints' schemas byte-for-byte consistent for this screen and matching the task's own stated preference for schema consistency with /analysis absent a good reason not to.
